overview.description: Buki Dominoes is an Austrian gambling domino game in which four players use a domino tile set, place stakes against a banker, and try to be the first to play all of their tiles or finish with the lowest pip total when the game blocks.
overview.originName: Bukidomino (German name used for Buki Dominoes)

history.origins:
Country/Region of Origin: Austria
Historical Context: Buki is a money game variant of Austrian Dominoes described in mid-20th-century Austrian sources, played with a banker and stakes.
Cultural Notes: Treated as a gambling game under Austrian law and played socially for money.
timeline: 1830: Early Austrian domino games with the double eight set documented by F. Tendler.
1960: Fritz Beck describes Austrian domino games and the gambling variant Buki using a reduced double eight set.
Late 20th century: Buki continues as a niche Austrian money game among domino players.

nullReasons.evolution: No clear evidence of rule evolution beyond the money-game framing; main structure is stable across descriptions.
nullReasons.cultural: No broader cultural role beyond being a local Austrian gambling variant of Austrian Dominoes.

Partnerships: None; each player plays for themselves against the banker.
setup.deck:
Type: Double-six style domino set (28 tiles)
Number of Sets: 1
Jokers: Not used; tiles are standard dominoes with pip values from 0 to 6.
setup.equipment: One domino tile set, stakes or chips for betting, and table space to lay out the Stamm and tableau.
setup.dealing:
Tiles per Player: 6 in the basic form, or 7 in the common variation; remaining tiles form the three-column Stamm or a single row used to mark betting positions.
Dealing Pattern: Clockwise; banker lays out the Stamm after players draw their tiles.

engine.deckDescription: One standard 28-tile double-six domino set. Each tile has two ends showing zero to six pips; every combination from 0-0 through 6-6 appears exactly once. No playing cards or jokers; used for Buki dominoes (and similar block or draw variants) where tiles are matched at the layout ends.
engine.suitDescription: Tiles are matched by pip value at the open ends of the layout. There are no traditional suits; each end value zero through six can connect to any tile sharing that value on one of its two ends.
engine.rankDescription: There is no rank hierarchy between tiles; play legality is determined by matching the pip value at an open end. Doubles (same pips on both ends) may be played crosswise. The first player to empty their hand (or the lowest total) wins as per the variant.

synthesis.shortDescription: Buki Dominoes is a domino card game that involves tiles, matching, scoring. The game originated in China and has become popular worldwide.

scoring.description: Each hand is settled for money: the player who dominoes, or who has the lowest total pips in hand when play is blocked, wins the bets they placed against the banker.
scoring.winCondition: Win individual games by playing your last tile or, in a blocked game, by having the lowest pip total; settle stakes between each non-banker and the banker according to the agreed minimum and maximum bets.

nullReasons.targetScore: No cumulative target score; Buki is settled per hand using stakes between each player and the banker.
nullReasons.scoringDirection: There is no single monotonic score track; each hand pays out stakes to the winner while others lose their bets, so high-versus-low score direction does not apply.
nullReasons.cardValues: Individual tiles do not award fixed point values; outcomes are based on pip totals in hand and the monetary stakes at the end of each game.
